I've never seen anything like this. OpenCat is an open source framework where Arduino based quadruped robots run Boston Dynamics style gaits, balance on slopes, and execute backflips from a single codebase. Any Bittle or Nybble boots with one flash. Reads the skill library. Calibrates the IMU. Starts walking, running, jumping, or sitting on command. The framework handles the hard parts: gait coordination across 12 servos, IMU sensor fusion for balance, and a skill library you extend without rewriting the core. Sensors clip in and go. Cameras, ultrasonic, touch, whatever you need. Researchers train reinforcement learning policies in NVIDIA Isaac Sim and deploy them to physical hardware the same afternoon. Others run visual and LiDAR SLAM through ROS, wire Bittle to ChatGPT for voice control, or manage IoT robot fleets on AWS. Built by Dr. Rongzhong Li in his Wake Forest dorm in 2016. Now one of the most starred quadruped projects on GitHub. → 5.2k stars, 611 forks → 30,000+ robots shipped across 60+ countries → Cited in 20+ academic papers → Multi language: C/C++, Python, block based → MIT licensed https://t.co/KBNFWB0d3L
